chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Bus tours and the Texas motorcycle patrolmen
summary: Touring Alabama, Louisiana and Texas by bus; two patrolmen stopped the band and made them play for them.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Oh, during the summertime we would make tours, like, through parts of Alabama, Louisiana, and East Texas, and different places in Mississippi... Even during the school-time, we would go out and do weekend gigs, like up in Northern Mississippi, like Clarksdale or Tupelo. I could run out and do those type things, or play down in Natchez or some place like that, you know. But we'd go on a tour, we called it a tour, going through Louisiana and Texas
and Alabama, and some parts of Arkansas.

That was quite an experience, you know, being on the bus out there, traveling with the guys. I'll never forget, one time we were going through Texas, and these two motorcycle patrolmen stopped the bus; you know, they flagged us down and they stopped the bus. And so, they asked... They said, "Oh, you guys a band, huh?" We said, "Yeah, we play music." Then one of them asked us where we were going, and we told them where we were going. So they asked one of the guys, said, "What do you play?" He told them. "Well, get it out." First thing they know, they had enough guys out...they made our guys get the instruments out and sit there and play for them before we could go any farther. We had to sit there and play for them. [LAUGHS HEARTILY] And after that, they cut us loose; we went out about our business, you know. But we had to play for them. [LAUGHS]
Yeah, it was pretty wild in those days, you know.
Yeah, we had our own bus; yeah, mmm-hmm.
